The shrine was formerly a prefectural shrine and is currently listed as a special shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].

It is one of the {{ill|Chichibu Three Shrines|ja|秩父三社|qid=Q140446060}}, along with {{ill|Chichibu Shrine|en|Chichibu Shrine|qid=Q2963366|lt=Chichibu Shrine}} and {{ill|Mitsumine Shrine|ja|三峯神社}}. The Okumiya (rear shrine) is located at the summit of Mount Hodo.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following three deities:
* '''{{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}''' (Kan'yamato Iwarehiko no Mikoto)
* '''{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祗神}}''' (Ōyama-tsumi no Kami)
* '''{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|ja|火産霊神|lt=Kagutsuchi}}''' (Homusubi no Kami)

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, in the 41st year of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}'s reign (111 AD), the Emperor's son, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}}, while on an expedition to the east, prayed at the mountain summit. A giant dog appeared and guided him to the summit. Along the way, they encountered a fierce fire from the northeast. The dog bravely jumped into the fire, extinguishing it, allowing Prince Yamato Takeru to safely reach the summit and pray. The prince, grateful for the dog's help, enshrined the deity of fire protection, Kagutsuchi, along with Ōyamatsumi, the god of the mountain, at the mountain base. This event is considered the origin of the shrine.

In May 2011, the shrine was awarded one star in the French edition of the "Michelin Green Guide Japon."

The {{ill|Aioi no Matsu|ja|相生の松|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582262}} (Aioi Pine) is believed to bring good fortune in love.

* From {{ill|Hanazono interchange|ja|花園インターチェンジ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11615194}} on the {{ill|Kan-etsu Expressway|en|Kan-etsu Expressway|qid=Q1059893|lt=Kan-Etsu Expressway}}, take {{ill|Japan National Route 140|en|Japan National Route 140|qid=Q6156790|lt=National Route 140}} for about 20 minutes

{{underline|To the Okumiya (Mount Hodo summit)}}
* Take the {{ill|Hodosan Ropeway|ja|宝登山ロープウェイ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宝登興業|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5876274}} from the foot station to the summit station, then walk approximately 5 minutes from the summit station

'''Nearby'''
* Gyokusenji Temple - founded in the first year of Eikyū (1113 AD){{sfn|New Musashi Fudoki Manuscript Fujiyabuchi Village|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿 藤谷淵村}}'s former betto temple
